endorsements.name: Harald Eilertsen
endorsements.label: CVE-2021-24375
endorsements.description: Lack of authentication or validation in motor_load_more, motor_gallery_load_more, motor_quick_view and motor_project_quick_view AJAX handlers of the Motor WordPress theme before 3.1.0 allows an unauthenticated attacker access to arbitrary files in the server file system, and to execute arbitrary php scripts found on the server file system. We found no vulnerability for uploading files with this theme, so any scripts to be executed must already be on the server file system.
endorsements.subtitle: CVE

endorsements.name: Harald Eilertsen
endorsements.label: CVE-2021-24499
endorsements.description: The Workreap WordPress theme before 2.2.2 AJAX actions workreap_award_temp_file_uploader and workreap_temp_file_uploader did not perform nonce checks, or validate that the request is from a valid user in any other way. The endpoints allowed for uploading arbitrary files to the uploads/workreap-temp directory. Uploaded files were neither sanitized nor validated, allowing an unauthenticated visitor to upload executable code such as php scripts.
endorsements.subtitle: CVE

povs.explanation: A published CVE record provides public, independently verifiable recognition of the credited vulnerability disclosure.

endorsements.name: Harald Eilertsen
endorsements.label: CVE-2021-24500
endorsements.description: Several AJAX actions available in the Workreap WordPress theme before 2.2.2 lacked CSRF protections, as well as allowing insecure direct object references that were not validated. This allows an attacker to trick a logged in user to submit a POST request to the vulnerable site, potentially modifying or deleting arbitrary objects on the target site.
endorsements.subtitle: CVE

endorsements.name: Harald Eilertsen
endorsements.label: CVE-2021-24501
endorsements.description: The Workreap WordPress theme before 2.2.2 had several AJAX actions missing authorization checks to verify that a user was authorized to perform critical operations such as modifying or deleting objects. This allowed a logged in user to modify or delete objects belonging to other users on the site.
